data.cultural_impact: The name Shufaiq holds a significant cultural impact as it symbolizes a source of brightness, guidance, and hope for Muslims. The name is often associated with the Prophet Ibrahim's (Abraham) vision of the full moon and the star (Al-Najm) mentioned in Surah Al-An'am, verse 78. The prophet's followers would name their children Shufaiq to remember this story and its message of guidance and divine intervention.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Shufaiq carries deep meaning in Islamic teachings. The name evokes the idea of being a light in the darkness, guiding others to the path of righteousness. It is a reminder that every Muslim has the potential to be a beacon of hope and light in their community. Furthermore, the name is also a reminder of the beauty and radiance of the divine light of Allah illuminating the hearts of those who believe in Him.

historical_references.context: The name Shufaiq is mentioned in connection with the Battle of Hunayn (630 AD), in which the Prophet Muhammad led an army against the Banu Hawazin and their allies. The name is given to a well-known companion, Al-Harith ibn Hisham Al-Ghifari, who was one of the leaders of the Hawazin. The name Shufaiq is believed to have been a nickname given to him due to his reddish complexion.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Al-Tabari's Tarikh Al-Rusul Wa Al- Muluk The name Shufaiq carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: The name Shufaiq is also mentioned in relation to a Battle of Uhud (625 AD) hero, Sa'd ibn Mu'adh Al-Khudri, who was known as Sa'd Al-Shufaiq.
